Glaser Rounds
Combat
Ammo. Only usable before resolution of a gun's strike.
This gun inflicts +2 damage each strike for the remainder
of this combat. Not usable the first time the gun is used
in a given combat. No more than 1 ammo card can be used
on a gun card each combat.

Kpist m/45
Equipment
Cost: 3 pool
Weapon. Gun.1R damage each strike, with an optional
maneuver each combat. When bearer strikes with this gun,
he or she gets an optional additional strike this round,
only usable to strike with this gun.

Add magazine; will rush. (Has anyone out there worked
with this combo yet?)

Fred

Hello,

I've played a wall deck based on this combo with !Malks (Marice
Fauvigny & Korah, Kite is also an option etc.). Obf/dem combo card
combat and a few Kindred Spirits to pay for the Kpist(s), Sibyl's
tongue for getting the right cards (also helps in getting Eternal
Vigilance, Blessing of Chaos) etc.

Being a wall helps with Glaser Rounds. The Kindred Spirits technic
also has the benefit of making your opponents to mistake your deck for
S&B! Oh, wait... I thought !Malks would just be the best clan to use
it overall (other combat options/ crypt selection considered), but
dunno.

Anyway, I think it takes a lot of cards. I've played it two or three
times and I feel it would be better just to use Disguised Weaon +
AK-47 instead of the DW+Kpist+Mag+Glaser mayhem and increase the
number of Kindred Spirits. But the deck/idea has certain charm... and
thematic appeal.

Best,

Heikki P.

Bleh. Swallowed. I missed the Swallowed. (Damn combo cards!) Swallowed

Your deck has a decent source of maneuver.

> And I agree, but using Celerity kinda makes the
> Kpist/Glaser/Magazine combo reduntant... Magnum + simple additional
> strike like pursuit becomes better option than Kpist + Glaser +
> Magazine hassle IMO (given the availability of CEL crypt options and
> Psyche! - Flash for cel).

Oh, I don't agree. The advantage in the K/G/M combo is that you don't
have to pack additional strike cards at all. Just Flashes. And, yes,
Psyche!s, I suppose. I think that would make your card flow a lot more
fluid. I'm not sure whether this works better than just .44s with
additional strikes in the end or not. And if it works better, does
that make it worth the extra pool and the need to used Disguised rather
Concealed? I dunno. It's something different though.

> It has less moving parts and is cheaper (equipment/cards/crypt
> options).

I agree with the latter but I don't see how you get the former. Flash
alone is _much_ better than mixing Flash and Pursuit if you don't need
the additional strike. You can Flash/press and Flash/maneuver (or
Psyche!/press and Flash/maneuver if that's your hand) and strike/strike
for four on subsequent rounds rather than Flash/press, Flash or Pursuit/
maneuver, and Pursuit/additional strike for six (assuming you've set up
with the Magizine/Glaser rounds). For six cards, you do 12 damage either
way and my way seems more fluid/less vulnerable to cards coming up in the
wrong order (but obviously has costs).

It's just setting up the K/G/M combo that's the weak part.

Fred

Ok. I tend see it in a way that (with Magnum) you can put Pursuit in
the deck instead (Kpist +) Glaser Rounds and Magazines - a reasonable
amount ( [guns equal]+6+4 =[x]+10 or something) makes (Magnum +)
Pursuit look much better/versatile in my eyes - it leaves slots for
other cards. When using a Magnum + celerity you also get other
versatile options like dodges etc., Kpist/Mag/Ammo practically ties
you to just "maneuver to long-shoot-shoot" -style combat.

> > It has less moving parts and is cheaper (equipment/cards/crypt
> > options).
>
> I agree with the latter but I don't see how you get the former. Flash
> alone is _much_ better than mixing Flash and Pursuit if you don't need
> the additional strike. You can Flash/press and Flash/maneuver (or
> Psyche!/press and Flash/maneuver if that's your hand) and strike/strike
> for four on subsequent rounds rather than Flash/press, Flash or Pursuit/
> maneuver, and Pursuit/additional strike for six (assuming you've set up
> with the Magizine/Glaser rounds). For six cards, you do 12 damage either
> way and my way seems more fluid/less vulnerable to cards coming up in the
> wrong order (but obviously has costs).

When talking about Celerity in the offensive I always take Psyche!
into account - for me, Pursuit + Psyche! beats Flash in most
occasions. And MEN don't mix Flash and Pursuit (they also play
Parmenides... and mono-Sennadurek) :P But I won't go to Flash vs.
Pursuit argument here.

I see the benefits you described in the card flow, but still... the
problem with the flow comes from the Kpist/Mag/Glaser angle (as you
mention later). Assuming a set up Magnum + Pursuit + Psyche = 6 damage
for just 2 cards (2 x Psyche! gives the same). So, for Celerity I see
other, better options. But that's me.

Kpist with the referred setup gives permanent 4 damage in the first
round without cards... But so does Assault Rifle :D An AK-47 also
gives the advantage of additional strike and eliminates the need for
Glasers (10 vs. 8 in two rounds is not very different in practice)...
but AR and AK-47 cost 5 pool. So, I tend to see Kpist (+ the combo) as
an option to play reasonably efficient/cheap gun combat for clans
without Celerity.

> It's just setting up the K/G/M combo that's the weak part.
>
> Fred

Indeed. I still think it's a bit too complicated setup for the benefit
and I probably agree with you in most points anyway. The Kpist/Mag/
Glaser combo is efficient in it's own way, and the variety aspect has
a value in itself (to me, at least).

I might ponder more about the Celerity angle you brought up, also
other options, perhaps... Now if Kpist/m45 cost 2 pool... :D

Best,

Heikki P.

Messages.Author: nys...@cs.com
Messages.Body:
On May 23, 5:41 pm, XZealot <xzea...@cox.net> wrote:
> 2 + 2 = 1 +3
>
> One is not better than the other.
>
> a second addtional strike for 3 which cannot be dodged is better than
> a second additional strike for 2

Good point.

However, if you think of it defensively, 2 + 2 can be better. If your
opponent has celerity and 2 blood, you can prevent him from playing
"blur" for additional strikes (which he may want to use to damage you,
rather than dodge). If he has one blood, 2+2 can send him into torpor
and prevent him from playing any additional strikes at all.

It does not manage how many additional strikes you get, if your
opponent does enough damage to you in the first strike.
